title: Berge's conjecture on path partitions
exact_target:
Can every minimum-cost directed path partition be matched by a
partial stable-set colouring that meets each path in the prescribed number of distinct colours?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
Let $D=(V,A)$ be a finite loopless digraph and $k\ge1$. A directed path
has distinct vertices and follows the directions of its successive arcs;
a single vertex is permitted. A path partition $\Pi$ consists of
vertex-disjoint directed paths covering $V$. Define its $k$-cost by
\[
                         c_k(\Pi)=\sum_{P\in\Pi}\min\{|V(P)|,k\}.
\]
A partial $k$-colouring is a collection $I_1,\ldots,I_k$ of pairwise
disjoint stable vertex sets, some possibly empty. Stability means that
no arc in either direction joins two vertices in the same set; vertices
outside their union remain uncoloured.

Berge's conjecture states that every path partition minimizing $c_k$
admits such a partial colouring with
\[
 |V(P)\cap(I_1\cup\cdots\cup I_k)|=\min\{|V(P)|,k\},
 \qquad |V(P)\cap I_j|\le1
\]
for every $P\in\Pi$ and every colour $j$.
Thus each path meets the required number of distinct colour classes.
The quantifier concerns every minimum-cost partition, not the existence
of one particularly convenient optimum. The paths are not required to
be induced, longest individually, or of equal length. A bound on the
total number of coloured vertices alone would miss the stipulated
compatibility with each separate path of the given partition.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Can every minimum-cost directed path partition be matched by a
partial stable-set colouring that meets each path in the prescribed number of distinct colours?
